significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that concept computation and language re-binding are causally separable, that most specified cross-lingual failures arise at the latter stage, and that the "binding failure rate grows monotonically with script/typological distance while concept-stage accuracy varies far less than end-task accuracy"; this combines a form-(ii) causal decomposition with a form-(iii) ordering and invariance across languages. That conclusion would constrain where multilingual failures should occur and whether inference-time correction or additional concept training is appropriate; this is load-bearing because Wendler et al.'s ACL 2024 study Do Llamas Work in English? supports shared, partly English-centric intermediate representations but leaves error localization as a consequential issue. The claim establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, while a negative result is also informative: entanglement would invalidate the two-stage ledger, and concept-dominated failures would instead support genuine reasoning weakness requiring training or data interventions. Topic substitution fails: the broad multilingual-representation topic alone would not warrant this score, whereas the specific per-failure decomposition and distance-dependent law place the claim above the obvious shared-middle/language-specific-late hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "Binding Ledger, a per-failure causal attribution protocol" and a "training-free late-layer language-vector correction"; the ledger is post hoc because it partitions observed failures, while the correction can be ex ante when applied as "one extra activation edit per forward pass" before an answer is produced. Re-extraction on another covered model would provide more than a search procedure if the asserted monotonic distance relation holds, because it predicts an ordering of binding-failure rates, although the hypothesis explicitly limits that prediction to "the tested models/tasks" rather than model families generally. Downstream uptake includes multilingual evaluators and product teams that could distinguish "reasoned right but spoke wrong" from concept failure and choose inference-time correction rather than retraining. Topic substitution fails: the topic by itself supplies neither this diagnostic partition nor a deployable correction, but the bounded scope and dependence on per-model re-extraction keep the reach below the highest bands.
